hints.title: Weighted Signal Latency Obstacle
hints.text: Signals propagate along directed network links with varying positive traversal times. How can greedily processing the smallest accumulated arrival time guarantee earliest signal reception across all nodes?

hints.title: Greedy Shortest Distance Invariant
hints.text: Extracting the unvisited node with the minimum tentative signal arrival time guarantees that its distance is final because all edge weights are strictly positive.

hints.title: Dijkstra Shortest Path Procedure
hints.text: Build an adjacency list adj[u] = list of (time, v). Maintain min-arrival distances mapping dist with source node k at time 0. Push (0, k) into a min-priority collection. While collection has entries: pop (d, u). If d > dist[u], continue. For each (w, v) from u: if d + w < dist.get(v, inf), record dist[v] = d + w and push (d + w, v). Return max(dist.values()) if len(dist) == n else -1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: E: number of directed edges (1 <= E <= 6000)
complexity.notes: Min-heap operations take logarithmic time per edge relaxation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Bellman-Ford or unweighted level searches incur redundant passes across dense network edges.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Adjacency graph and priority heap consume O(V + E) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using Dijkstra's algorithm for non-negative edge weights and checking all nodes were reached.
